en: The verb changes to match the subject: am, is, are.
tr: Fiil özneye göre değişir: am, is, are.
fa: فعل با فاعل عوض می‌شود: am، is، are.

en: After I, he or we you can leave out am/is/are.
tr: I, he, we'den sonra am/is/are atlanabilir.
fa: بعد از I، he، we می‌شود am/is/are را حذف کرد.

en: Use 'is' for every subject.
tr: Her özne için 'is' kullanılır.
fa: برای همهٔ فاعل‌ها از is استفاده می‌شود.

en: “I am from Iran and my sister is a nurse.” The rule: English always needs a form of be (am, is, are) between the subject and what comes after it. Use am with I, is with he, she and it, and are with you, we and they; the table below shows every form. In Turkish or Persian an ending can do this job, but English never leaves be out. Remember: “She is tired”, not “She tired”.
tr: “I am from Iran and my sister is a nurse.” Kural: İngilizcede özne ile ondan sonra gelen kısım arasında her zaman be fiilinin bir biçimi (am, is, are) bulunur. I ile am, he, she ve it ile is, you, we ve they ile are kullan; bütün biçimler aşağıdaki tabloda. Türkçede bu işi bir ek görebilir, İngilizce ise be'yi asla atlamaz. Unutma: “She tired” değil, “She is tired”.
fa: “I am from Iran and my sister is a nurse.” قاعده: در انگلیسی بین فاعل و بخشِ بعد از آن همیشه یک شکل از فعل be (am, is, are) لازم است. با I از am، با he، she و it از is و با you، we و they از are استفاده کن؛ همهٔ شکل‌ها در جدول پایین است. در فارسی گاهی یک پسوند همین کار را می‌کند، ولی انگلیسی هیچ‌وقت be را حذف نمی‌کند. یادت باشد: “She is tired”، نه “She tired”.

en: Every sentence needs a subject before the verb.
tr: Her cümlede fiilden önce bir özne olmalı.
fa: هر جمله قبل از فعل یک فاعل لازم دارد.

en: The verb ending shows who, so no subject is needed.
tr: Fiil eki kimi gösterir, özneye gerek yok.
fa: پایان فعل می‌گوید چه کسی، پس فاعل لازم نیست.

en: Use 'him' or 'her' as the subject.
tr: Özne olarak 'him' ya da 'her' kullanılır.
fa: به‌عنوان فاعل از him یا her استفاده می‌شود.

en: Every English sentence needs a subject before the verb: She is my sister. The rule: put the subject first and the verb after it; if we already know the person or thing, the subject can be a pronoun. Subject pronouns: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Use he for a man, she for a woman, it for a thing or an animal, and they for two or more. Remember: never start with the verb — say “He is late”, not “Is late”.
tr: İngilizcede her cümlenin fiilden önce bir öznesi olmalı: She is my sister. Kural: önce özne, sonra fiil gelir; kişiyi ya da şeyi zaten biliyorsak özne bir zamir olabilir. Özne zamirleri: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Türkçedeki “o” burada üçe ayrılır: erkek için he, kadın için she ve eşya ya da hayvan için it. İki ya da daha fazla kişi veya şey için they kullanılır. Unutma: Türkçede “Geliyor” tek başına bir cümledir, İngilizcede ise özne şart — “Is coming” değil, “She is coming”.
fa: در انگلیسی هر جمله قبل از فعل یک فاعل لازم دارد: She is my sister. قاعده: اول فاعل می‌آید و بعد فعل؛ اگر معلوم است از چه کسی یا چه چیزی حرف می‌زنیم، فاعل می‌تواند یک ضمیر باشد. ضمیرهای فاعلی: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. «او»ی فارسی در انگلیسی دوتاست: برای مرد he و برای زن she؛ برای شیء یا حیوان it و برای دو نفر یا بیشتر they. یادت باشد: در فارسی «می‌آید» به‌تنهایی یک جمله است، ولی در انگلیسی فاعل لازم است — “She is coming”، نه “Is coming”.

en: A few nouns change shape in the plural: child → children.
tr: Bazı isimler çoğulda şekil değiştirir: child → children.
fa: بعضی اسم‌ها در جمع شکل عوض می‌کنند: child ← children.

en: Add -s to every noun: childs, mans.
tr: Her isme -s eklenir: childs, mans.
fa: به هر اسمی -s اضافه می‌شود: childs، mans.

en: After a number the noun stays singular: two child.
tr: Sayıdan sonra isim tekil kalır: two child.
fa: بعد از عدد اسم مفرد می‌ماند: two child.

en: One book, two books: most nouns just add -s. The rule: when there is more than one, the noun takes -s (or -es or -ies, as in the spelling below). Spelling: cats, buses, boxes, cities, babies. Add -es after -s, -x, -sh and -ch, and change consonant + y to -ies. A few common nouns change shape: child → children, man → men, woman → women, person → people, foot → feet. Remember: after any number bigger than one, the noun is plural — “two books”, not “two book”.
tr: One book, two books: çoğu isim sadece -s alır. Kural: birden fazla şey varsa isim -s alır (ya da aşağıdaki yazılışa göre -es veya -ies). Yazılış: cats, buses, boxes, cities, babies. Sonu -s, -x, -sh ve -ch olan isimlere -es ekle; ünsüz + y ise -ies olur. Bazı yaygın isimler şekil değiştirir: child → children, man → men, woman → women, person → people, foot → feet. Unutma: Türkçede “iki kitap” deriz, ama İngilizcede birden büyük her sayıdan sonra isim çoğuldur — “two book” değil, “two books”.
fa: One book, two books: بیشتر اسم‌ها فقط ‎-s می‌گیرند. قاعده: وقتی بیشتر از یکی است، اسم ‎-s می‌گیرد (یا طبق املای پایین ‎-es یا ‎-ies). املا: cats, buses, boxes, cities, babies. بعد از ‎-s، ‎-x، ‎-sh و ‎-ch باید ‎-es بگذاری، و حرف بی‌صدا + y می‌شود ‎-ies. چند اسم پرکاربرد شکلشان عوض می‌شود: child / children, man / men, woman / women, person / people, foot / feet. یادت باشد: در فارسی می‌گوییم «دو کتاب»، ولی در انگلیسی بعد از هر عدد بزرگ‌تر از یک، اسم جمع است — “two books”، نه “two book”.

en: One near = this, many near = these; far = that / those.
tr: Yakında bir = this, çok = these; uzakta = that / those.
fa: یکی نزدیک = this، چندتا نزدیک = these؛ دور = that / those.

en: 'This' works for one thing or many things.
tr: 'This' hem bir şey hem çok şey için kullanılır.
fa: this هم برای یک چیز و هم چند چیز به کار می‌رود.

en: 'These' is for things far away.
tr: 'These' uzaktaki şeyler içindir.
fa: these برای چیزهای دور است.

en: Hold up your phone and say “this is my phone”; look at a car across the street and say “that is a car”. The rule: this / these for things near you, that / those for things far away; these and those are plural. Near you: this for one thing, these for more than one. Far from you: that for one thing, those for more than one. Remember: these and those need are and a plural noun — “Those are my parents”, not “That is my parents”.
tr: Telefonunu göster ve “this is my phone” de; karşıdaki bir arabaya bak ve “that is a car” de. Kural: yakındaki şeyler için this / these, uzaktakiler için that / those; these ve those çoğuldur. Yakındakiler: tek şey için this, birden fazla için these. Uzaktakiler: tek şey için that, birden fazla için those. Unutma: these ve those ile fiil are olur ve isim çoğuldur — “That is my parents” değil, “Those are my parents”.
fa: گوشی‌ات را نشان بده و بگو “this is my phone”؛ به ماشینی آن طرف خیابان نگاه کن و بگو “that is a car”. قاعده: برای چیزهای نزدیک this / these و برای چیزهای دور that / those؛ these و those جمع‌اند. نزدیک: برای یک چیز this، برای بیشتر از یکی these. دور: برای یک چیز that، برای بیشتر از یکی those. یادت باشد: در فارسی می‌گوییم «این کتاب‌ها» و «این» عوض نمی‌شود، ولی در انگلیسی برای جمع باید these بگویی — “These books are new”، نه “This books are new”.

en: Only he, she and it add -s to the verb.
tr: Sadece he, she, it fiile -s ekler.
fa: فقط he، she و it به فعل -s می‌دهند.

en: Add -s to the verb for every subject.
tr: Her özne için fiile -s eklenir.
fa: برای هر فاعلی به فعل -s اضافه می‌شود.

en: Add -s when the subject is plural: they goes.
tr: Özne çoğulsa -s eklenir: they goes.
fa: وقتی فاعل جمع است -s می‌آید: they goes.

en: Compare: I work, you work, they work — but she works. The rule: in the present simple, the verb takes -s only after he, she or it. Use it for habits and routines; a name or one thing, like Anna or my car, works like he, she or it. Spelling: works, goes, watches, finishes, studies. Add -es after -o, -sh, -ch, -s and -x, and change consonant + y to -ies. Remember: have becomes has — “She has a cat”, not “She haves a cat”.
tr: Karşılaştır: I work, you work, they work — ama she works. Kural: geniş zamanda fiil yalnızca he, she ya da it'ten sonra -s alır. Bunu alışkanlıklar ve rutinler için kullan; Anna ya da my car gibi bir isim veya tek bir şey de he, she, it gibi davranır. Yazılış: works, goes, watches, finishes, studies. Sonu -o, -sh, -ch, -s ve -x olan fiillere -es ekle; ünsüz + y ise -ies olur. Unutma: have, he / she / it ile has olur — “She haves a cat” değil, “She has a cat”.
fa: مقایسه کن: I work, you work, they work — ولی she works. قاعده: در حال ساده فقط بعد از he، she یا it به فعل ‎-s اضافه می‌شود. از آن برای عادت‌ها و کارهای هر روز استفاده کن؛ یک اسم یا یک چیز، مثل Anna یا my car، هم مثل he، she و it است. املا: works, goes, watches, finishes, studies. اگر فعل به ‎-o، ‎-sh، ‎-ch، ‎-s یا ‎-x تمام شود ‎-es می‌گیرد، و حرف بی‌صدا + y می‌شود ‎-ies. یادت باشد: have با he / she / it می‌شود has — “She has a cat”، نه “She haves a cat”.

en: The owner word goes right before the noun: my car.
tr: Sahiplik sözcüğü ismin hemen önüne gelir: my car.
fa: کلمهٔ مالکیت درست قبل از اسم می‌آید: my car.

en: The owner word comes after the noun: car my.
tr: Sahiplik sözcüğü isimden sonra gelir: car my.
fa: کلمهٔ مالکیت بعد از اسم می‌آید: car my.

en: Use 'you' or 'us' before the noun: you bag.
tr: İsimden önce 'you' ya da 'us' kullanılır: you bag.
fa: قبل از اسم از you یا us استفاده می‌شود: you bag.

en: To show who owns something, put a small owner word right before the thing: my car, her bag. The rule: choose the word for the owner, not for the thing, and put it before the noun. Possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her, its, our, their. So Ali's mother is “his mother”, and Sara's father is “her father”. Remember: the owner word always comes first — “my car”, not “car my”.
tr: Bir şeyin kime ait olduğunu söylemek için sahip kelimesini eşyanın hemen önüne koy: my car, her bag. Kural: kelimeyi eşyaya göre değil sahibe göre seç ve ismin önüne koy. İyelik sıfatları: my, your, his, her, its, our, their. Yani Ali'nin annesi “his mother”, Sara'nın babası “her father” olur. Unutma: Türkçede “arabam” deyip eki kullanırız, İngilizcede ise ayrı bir kelime gerekir — “car” değil, “my car”.
fa: برای اینکه بگویی چیزی مال کیست، کلمهٔ مالک را درست قبل از آن چیز بگذار: my car, her bag. قاعده: کلمه را بر اساس صاحب انتخاب کن، نه خودِ آن چیز، و آن را قبل از اسم بگذار. صفت‌های ملکی: my, your, his, her, its, our, their. پس مادرِ علی می‌شود “his mother” و پدرِ سارا می‌شود “her father”. یادت باشد: در فارسی می‌گوییم «ماشینِ من»، ولی در انگلیسی ترتیب برعکس است — “my car”، نه “car my”.

en: To say something exists, start with 'there' + is / are.
tr: Bir şeyin var olduğunu söylemek için 'there' + is / are.
fa: برای گفتن وجود چیزی، با there + is / are شروع کن.

en: Start with 'It is' to say something exists.
tr: Bir şeyin varlığı için cümleye 'It is' ile başlanır.
fa: برای گفتن وجود چیزی با It is شروع می‌کنیم.

en: 'There is' works for one thing or many.
tr: 'There is' hem tek hem çok şey için kullanılır.
fa: There is هم برای یکی هم برای چندتا به کار می‌رود.

en: To say that something is in a place, start with there: There is a café next to the station. The rule: there is + one thing, there are + more than one. Forms: there is, there are, is there, are there. In a question, the two words swap: Is there a bank near here? Remember: don't start with the place — say “There is a supermarket on my street”, not “On my street is a supermarket”.
tr: Bir yerde bir şeyin olduğunu söylemek için there ile başla: There is a café next to the station. Kural: tek şey için there is, birden fazlası için there are. Biçimler: there is, there are, is there, are there. Soruda iki kelimenin yeri değişir: Is there a bank near here? Unutma: Türkçedeki “var” İngilizcede there is / there are olur — “On my street is a supermarket” değil, “There is a supermarket on my street”.
fa: برای اینکه بگویی چیزی جایی هست، جمله را با there شروع کن: There is a café next to the station. قاعده: برای یک چیز there is و برای بیشتر از یکی there are. شکل‌ها: there is, there are, is there, are there. در سؤال جای این دو کلمه عوض می‌شود: Is there a bank near here? یادت باشد: «هست» فارسی در انگلیسی می‌شود there is / there are — “There is a supermarket on my street”، نه “On my street is a supermarket”.

en: in = inside, on = on top, under = below.
tr: in = içinde, on = üstünde, under = altında.
fa: in = داخل، on = روی، under = زیر.

en: 'in' works for anything near a table or sofa.
tr: 'in' masa ya da koltuğun yakınındaki her şey için olur.
fa: in برای هر چیزی نزدیک میز یا مبل به کار می‌رود.

en: 'on' means inside a box or a room.
tr: 'on' bir kutunun ya da odanın içinde demektir.
fa: on یعنی داخل یک جعبه یا اتاق.

en: Where are your keys? In your bag, on the table or under the sofa? The rule: choose the word by the position: inside, on top, below or beside. Place words: in, on, under, next to, behind, in front of. In means inside, on means on top of a surface, under means below, and next to means beside. Use at for a point: at the door, at work, at home. Remember: a table is a surface, so things are on it — “on the table”, not “in the table”.
tr: Anahtarların nerede? Çantanın içinde mi, masanın üstünde mi, kanepenin altında mı? Kural: kelimeyi konuma göre seç: içinde, üstünde, altında ya da yanında. Yer kelimeleri: in, on, under, next to, behind, in front of. In içinde, on bir yüzeyin üstünde, under altında, next to yanında demektir. Bir nokta ya da bir şey yaptığın yer için at kullan: at the door, at work, at home. Unutma: Türkçede hepsi için “-de” eki yeter, İngilizcede ise yere göre kelime seçersin — masa bir yüzeydir, yani “in the table” değil, “on the table”.
fa: در انگلیسی جای هر چیز را با یک کلمهٔ کوچک می‌گوییم: in the bag, on the table, under the sofa. قاعده: کلمه را بر اساس جا انتخاب کن: داخل، روی، زیر یا کنار. کلمه‌های مکان: in, on, under, next to, behind, in front of. in یعنی داخل، on یعنی روی یک سطح، under یعنی زیر و next to یعنی کنار. برای یک نقطه یا جایی که در آن کاری می‌کنی at بگذار: at the door, at work, at home. یادت باشد: در فارسی «در» برای خیلی از این‌ها کافی است، ولی در انگلیسی میز یک سطح است — “on the table”، نه “in the table”.

en: 'an' before a vowel sound, 'a' before a consonant sound.
tr: Ünlü sesten önce 'an', ünsüz sesten önce 'a'.
fa: قبل از صدای مصوت an، قبل از صدای صامت a.

en: Jobs don't need 'a' or 'an': she is engineer.
tr: Mesleklerde 'a' / 'an' gerekmez: she is engineer.
fa: شغل‌ها a یا an لازم ندارند: she is engineer.

en: 'an' depends on the first letter, not the sound.
tr: 'an' sese değil, ilk harfe bağlıdır.
fa: an به حرف اول بستگی دارد، نه به صدا.

en: Before one person or thing, English needs a or an: I am a teacher. The rule: a before a consonant sound, an before a vowel sound. Examples: a car, a house, an apple, an hour, a university. Listen to the sound, not the letter: hour starts with an “ow” sound and university with a “you” sound. Remember: a job needs a / an too — “My brother is a doctor”, not “My brother is doctor”.
tr: İngilizcede tek bir kişi ya da şeyden önce a veya an gerekir: I am a teacher. Kural: ünsüz sesten önce a, ünlü sesten önce an. Örnekler: a car, a house, an apple, an hour, a university. Harfe değil, sese dikkat et: hour “av” sesiyle, university “yu” sesiyle başlar. Unutma: Türkçede “Abim doktor” deriz, İngilizcede meslekten önce de a / an gerekir — “My brother is doctor” değil, “My brother is a doctor”.
fa: در انگلیسی قبل از یک نفر یا یک چیز a یا an لازم است: I am a teacher. قاعده: قبل از صدای بی‌صدا a و قبل از صدای صدادار an. مثال‌ها: a car, a house, an apple, an hour, a university. به صدا گوش کن، نه به حرف: hour با صدای «آو» و university با صدای «یو» شروع می‌شود. یادت باشد: در فارسی می‌گوییم «برادرم دکتر است»، ولی در انگلیسی قبل از شغل هم a / an لازم است — “My brother is a doctor”، نه “My brother is doctor”.

en: In a question, is / are jumps in front of the subject.
tr: Soruda is / are öznenin önüne geçer.
fa: در سؤال، is / are جلوی فاعل می‌پرد.

en: Keep normal word order and just add '?'.
tr: Normal sıra kalır, sadece '?' eklenir.
fa: ترتیب عادی می‌ماند و فقط «؟» اضافه می‌شود.

en: The question word goes at the end: Your name is what?
tr: Soru sözcüğü sona gelir: Your name is what?
fa: کلمهٔ پرسشی آخر می‌آید: Your name is what?

en: A question starts with a question word: Why are you late? The rule: question word, then the verb or do / does, then the person. Question words: what, where, when, who, why, how. With am / is / are, the verb moves: they are / Where are they? With other verbs, use do, or does for he / she / it: What do you eat for breakfast? Remember: the verb or do comes right after the question word — “Where are you from?”, not “Where you are from?”.
tr: Soru bir soru kelimesiyle başlar: Why are you late? Kural: önce soru kelimesi, sonra fiil ya da do / does, sonra kişi gelir. Soru kelimeleri: what, where, when, who, why, how. Fiil am / is / are ise yer değiştirir: they are / Where are they? Başka fiillerde do kullan, he / she / it için does: What do you eat for breakfast? Unutma: Türkçede soru sorarken kelimelerin sırası değişmez (“Sen nerelisin?”), İngilizcede ise fiil ya da do soru kelimesinden hemen sonra gelir — “Where you are from?” değil, “Where are you from?”.
fa: سؤال با یک کلمهٔ پرسشی شروع می‌شود: Why are you late? قاعده: اول کلمهٔ پرسشی، بعد فعل یا do / does، بعد شخص. کلمه‌های پرسشی: what, where, when, who, why, how. اگر فعل am / is / are است، جایش عوض می‌شود: they are / Where are they? با فعل‌های دیگر do بیاور و برای he / she / it از does استفاده کن: What do you eat for breakfast? یادت باشد: در فارسی ترتیب کلمه‌ها در سؤال عوض نمی‌شود («کجا زندگی می‌کنی؟»)، ولی در انگلیسی فعل یا do درست بعد از کلمهٔ پرسشی می‌آید — “Where are you from?”، نه “Where you are from?”.

en: Use don't / doesn't to say no and do / does to ask; the main verb stays plain.
tr: Olumsuz için don't / doesn't, soru için do / does; asıl fiil yalın kalır.
fa: برای منفی don't / doesn't و برای سؤال do / does؛ فعل اصلی ساده می‌ماند.

en: Put not right after the person: I not like fish.
tr: not kişiden hemen sonra gelir: I not like fish.
fa: not درست بعد از شخص می‌آید: I not like fish.

en: Keep the -s after doesn't: she doesn't likes.
tr: doesn't'tan sonra da -s kalır: she doesn't likes.
fa: بعد از doesn't هم ‎-s می‌ماند: she doesn't likes.

en: Compare: I like tea, but I don't like coffee. The rule: don't / doesn't + base verb for negatives, do / does + person + base verb for questions. To say no, put don't before the verb; with he, she and it, use doesn't. To ask, put do or does before the person: Do you work here? Forms: don't, doesn't, do, does. Remember: does already has the -s, so the main verb stays plain — “Does he play?”, not “Does he plays?”.
tr: Karşılaştır: I like tea, but I don't like coffee. Kural: olumsuz için don't / doesn't + yalın fiil, soru için do / does + kişi + yalın fiil. Olumsuz için fiilden önce don't koy; he, she ve it ile doesn't kullan. Soru için kişiden önce do ya da does getir: Do you work here? Biçimler: don't, doesn't, do, does. Unutma: Türkçede olumsuzluğu fiile -me / -ma ekleyerek, soruyu da mi ile yaparız; İngilizcede ise do / does gerekir — “I not like fish” değil, “I don't like fish”.
fa: مقایسه کن: I like tea, but I don't like coffee. قاعده: برای منفی don't / doesn't + شکل سادهٔ فعل، برای سؤال do / does + شخص + شکل سادهٔ فعل. برای منفی کردن، قبل از فعل don't بگذار؛ با he، she و it از doesn't استفاده کن. برای سؤال، do یا does را قبل از شخص بیاور: Do you work here? شکل‌ها: don't, doesn't, do, does. یادت باشد: در فارسی سؤال را معمولاً فقط با لحن می‌سازیم («ماهی دوست داری؟»)، ولی در انگلیسی Do لازم است — “Do you like fish?”، نه “You like fish?”.

en: Regular verbs add -ed; irregular ones change: go → went.
tr: Düzenli fiiller -ed alır; düzensizler değişir: go → went.
fa: فعل‌های باقاعده -ed می‌گیرند؛ بی‌قاعده‌ها عوض می‌شوند: go ← went.

en: Every verb takes -ed in the past: goed, buyed.
tr: Geçmişte her fiil -ed alır: goed, buyed.
fa: در گذشته هر فعلی -ed می‌گیرد: goed، buyed.

en: Past actions use the base verb plus 'yesterday'.
tr: Geçmiş için yalın fiil + 'yesterday' yeter.
fa: برای گذشته فعل ساده + yesterday کافی است.

en: “Last Saturday we cleaned the flat and saw a film.” The rule: for a finished action in the past, add -ed to regular verbs and use the past form of irregular verbs. Regular: visit → visited, play → played, watch → watched. Many common verbs are irregular: go → went, buy → bought, eat → ate, have → had, see → saw. In questions and negatives, use did + base verb: Did you go? I didn't go. Remember: after did, no past form — “Did you see Ali?”, not “Did you saw Ali?”.
tr: “Last Saturday we cleaned the flat and saw a film.” Kural: geçmişte bitmiş bir eylem için düzenli fiillere -ed ekle, düzensiz fiillerin ise geçmiş biçimini kullan. Düzenli: visit → visited, play → played, watch → watched. Sık kullanılan birçok fiil düzensizdir: go → went, buy → bought, eat → ate, have → had, see → saw. Soru ve olumsuz cümlelerde did + yalın fiil kullan: Did you go? I didn't go. Unutma: did'den sonra geçmiş biçim gelmez — “Did you saw Ali?” değil, “Did you see Ali?”.
fa: “Last Saturday we cleaned the flat and saw a film.” قاعده: برای کاری که در گذشته تمام شده، به فعل‌های باقاعده ‎-ed اضافه کن و برای فعل‌های بی‌قاعده شکل گذشته‌شان را بیاور. باقاعده: visit / visited, play / played, watch / watched. خیلی از فعل‌های پرکاربرد بی‌قاعده‌اند: go / went, buy / bought, eat / ate, have / had, see / saw. در جملهٔ سؤالی و منفی، did + شکل سادهٔ فعل بیاور: Did you go? I didn't go. یادت باشد: بعد از did شکل گذشته نمی‌آید — “Did you see Ali?”، نه “Did you saw Ali?”.

en: Plans need three parts: be + going to + base verb.
tr: Planlar üç parça ister: be + going to + yalın fiil.
fa: برنامه سه بخش می‌خواهد: be + going to + فعل ساده.

en: 'Going to' works alone, without am / is / are.
tr: 'Going to' tek başına, am / is / are olmadan kullanılır.
fa: going to به‌تنهایی و بدون am / is / are کار می‌کند.

en: Use the present simple for plans: I go tomorrow.
tr: Planlar için geniş zaman: I go tomorrow.
fa: برای برنامه از حال ساده استفاده می‌شود: I go tomorrow.

en: “I'm going to paint my room this weekend — I've already bought the paint.” The rule: am / is / are + going to + base verb. Forms: I am going to, he / she / it is going to, you / we / they are going to. Use it for a plan you have already made, and for something you can see coming now: Be careful! That glass is going to fall. Remember: don't drop am / is / are — “We're going to call you tonight”, not “We going to call you tonight”.
tr: “I'm going to paint my room this weekend — I've already bought the paint.” Kural: am / is / are + going to + yalın fiil. Biçimler: I am going to, he / she / it is going to, you / we / they are going to. Bunu önceden kararını verdiğin bir plan için ve şu anda geldiğini gördüğün bir şey için kullan: Be careful! That glass is going to fall. Unutma: am / is / are'ı düşürme — “We going to call you tonight” değil, “We're going to call you tonight”.
fa: “I'm going to paint my room this weekend — I've already bought the paint.” قاعده: am / is / are + going to + شکل سادهٔ فعل. شکل‌ها: I am going to, he / she / it is going to, you / we / they are going to. از آن برای برنامه‌ای استفاده کن که از قبل تصمیمش را گرفته‌ای، و برای چیزی که همین الان می‌بینی دارد پیش می‌آید: Be careful! That glass is going to fall. یادت باشد: am / is / are را نینداز — “We're going to call you tonight”، نه “We going to call you tonight”.

en: Short adjectives take -er; long ones take 'more'.
tr: Kısa sıfatlar -er alır; uzunlar 'more' alır.
fa: صفت‌های کوتاه -er می‌گیرند؛ بلندها more.

en: Use 'more' with every adjective: more big.
tr: Her sıfatla 'more' kullanılır: more big.
fa: با هر صفتی more می‌آید: more big.

en: 'Good' becomes 'more good' or 'gooder'.
tr: 'Good' karşılaştırmada 'more good' ya da 'gooder' olur.
fa: good می‌شود more good یا gooder.

en: “My new flat is smaller than my old one, but it's cheaper.” The rule: to compare two things, add -er to a short adjective or put more before a long one, then use than. Short: tall → taller, cold → colder, cheap → cheaper. Long: more difficult, more interesting, more expensive. Spelling: big → bigger, hot → hotter, easy → easier. Two common ones are irregular: good → better, bad → worse. Never use more and -er together. Remember: one-syllable adjectives take -er — “This road is longer”, not “This road is more long”.
tr: “My new flat is smaller than my old one, but it's cheaper.” Kural: iki şeyi karşılaştırmak için kısa sıfata -er ekle ya da uzun sıfatın önüne more koy, sonra than kullan. Kısa: tall → taller, cold → colder, cheap → cheaper. Uzun: more difficult, more interesting, more expensive. Yazım: big → bigger, hot → hotter, easy → easier. Sık kullanılan iki sıfat düzensizdir: good → better, bad → worse. More ile -er'i asla birlikte kullanma. Türkçede her sıfatın önüne “daha” geldiği için more'u her yere koymak kolaydır. Unutma: tek heceli sıfatlar -er alır — “This road is more long” değil, “This road is longer”.
fa: “My new flat is smaller than my old one, but it's cheaper.” قاعده: برای مقایسهٔ دو چیز، به صفت کوتاه ‎-er اضافه کن یا قبل از صفت بلند more بیاور، و بعد than. کوتاه: tall / taller, cold / colder, cheap / cheaper. بلند: more difficult, more interesting, more expensive. املا: big / bigger, hot / hotter, easy / easier. دو صفت پرکاربرد بی‌قاعده‌اند: good / better, bad / worse. هیچ‌وقت more و ‎-er را با هم نیاور. در فارسی به هر صفتی «‌تر» اضافه می‌کنیم، ولی در انگلیسی صفت بلند ‎-er نمی‌گیرد و difficulter غلط است. یادت باشد: صفت یک‌هجایی ‎-er می‌گیرد — “This road is longer”، نه “This road is more long”.

en: The best of a group: the + -est or the + most.
tr: Grubun en'i: the + -est ya da the + most.
fa: برترینِ یک گروه: the + ‎-est یا the + most.

en: Use 'more' when you pick the winner of a group.
tr: Grubun birincisi için 'more' kullanılır.
fa: برای برندهٔ یک گروه از more استفاده می‌شود.

en: Superlatives never need 'the': most expensive hotel.
tr: En üstünlükte 'the' gerekmez: most expensive hotel.
fa: عالی‌ترین هرگز the نمی‌خواهد: most expensive hotel.

en: “It's the oldest café in the city and the most popular one, too.” The rule: to pick one from a group of three or more, use the + short adjective + -est, or the most + a long adjective. Short: the coldest, the fastest, the highest. Long: the most beautiful, the most expensive, the most famous. Spelling: big → the biggest, funny → the funniest. Irregular: good → the best, bad → the worst. Remember: the superlative always needs the — “It's the cheapest shop in town”, not “It's cheapest shop in town”.
tr: “It's the oldest café in the city and the most popular one, too.” Kural: üç ya da daha fazla şeyin içinden birini seçmek için the + kısa sıfat + -est ya da the most + uzun sıfat kullan. Kısa: the coldest, the fastest, the highest. Uzun: the most beautiful, the most expensive, the most famous. Yazım: big → the biggest, funny → the funniest. Düzensiz: good → the best, bad → the worst. Türkçede “en” yeterlidir ve “the” yoktur, bu yüzden the kolayca unutulur. Unutma: en üstünlük her zaman the ister — “It's cheapest shop in town” değil, “It's the cheapest shop in town”.
fa: “It's the oldest café in the city and the most popular one, too.” قاعده: برای انتخاب یکی از میان سه چیز یا بیشتر، the + صفت کوتاه + ‎-est یا the most + صفت بلند بیاور. کوتاه: the coldest, the fastest, the highest. بلند: the most beautiful, the most expensive, the most famous. املا: big / the biggest, funny / the funniest. بی‌قاعده: good / the best, bad / the worst. در فارسی «ترین» کافی است و حرف تعریف نداریم، برای همین the راحت جا می‌افتد. یادت باشد: صفت عالی همیشه the می‌خواهد — “It's the cheapest shop in town”، نه “It's cheapest shop in town”.

en: Positive and offers → some; negatives and questions → any.
tr: some = olumlu ve teklif; any = olumsuz ve soru.
fa: some = مثبت و تعارف؛ any = منفی و سؤال.

en: 'some' and 'any' mean the same and swap freely.
tr: 'some' ve 'any' aynıdır, serbestçe değişir.
fa: some و any یکی‌اند و آزادانه جابه‌جا می‌شوند.

en: 'any' is only for questions, never after 'not'.
tr: 'any' sadece sorudadır, 'not'tan sonra gelmez.
fa: any فقط در سؤال است، هرگز بعد از not نمی‌آید.

en: “There's some bread, but there isn't any butter.” The rule: use some in positive sentences, and any in negatives and most questions. Positive: I have some time, there are some apples. Negative: we don't have any plans, there aren't any apples. Questions: Is there any milk? Do you have any brothers? Offers and requests are different: they take some, because you expect a yes: Would you like some cake? Can I have some coffee? Remember: after not, use any — “We don't need any help”, not “We don't need some help”.
tr: “There's some bread, but there isn't any butter.” Kural: olumlu cümlelerde some, olumsuz cümlelerde ve çoğu soruda any kullan. Olumlu: I have some time, there are some apples. Olumsuz: we don't have any plans, there aren't any apples. Soru: Is there any milk? Do you have any brothers? İkram ve ricalar farklıdır: evet cevabı beklediğin için some alır: Would you like some cake? Can I have some coffee? Unutma: not'tan sonra any gelir — “We don't need some help” değil, “We don't need any help”.
fa: “There's some bread, but there isn't any butter.” قاعده: در جملهٔ مثبت some بیاور، و در جملهٔ منفی و بیشتر سؤال‌ها any. مثبت: I have some time, there are some apples. منفی: we don't have any plans, there aren't any apples. سؤال: Is there any milk? Do you have any brothers? تعارف و درخواست فرق دارد: چون انتظار «بله» داری، some می‌گیرد: Would you like some cake? Can I have some coffee? یادت باشد: بعد از not، any بیاور — “We don't need any help”، نه “We don't need some help”.

en: Right now you can; back then you could; never with 'to'.
tr: can = şimdi; could = geçmişte yapabilme; 'to' yok.
fa: can = توانایی الان؛ could = توانایی در گذشته؛ بدون to.

en: 'can' takes 'to': she can to drive.
tr: 'can' 'to' alır: she can to drive.
fa: can با to می‌آید: she can to drive.

en: 'can' also works for the past: she can swim at five.
tr: 'can' geçmiş için de olur: she can swim at five.
fa: can برای گذشته هم کار می‌کند: she can swim at five.

en: “I can't swim very well, but when I was a child I could swim for hours.” The rule: can + base verb is ability now; could + base verb is ability in the past. Negatives: can't, couldn't. Can is the same for every person, with no -s and no to: she can ski, he can cook. To ask for help, start with Can you ...?: Can you carry this box? Remember: no to after can or could — “He can play the guitar”, not “He can to play the guitar”.
tr: “I can't swim very well, but when I was a child I could swim for hours.” Kural: can + yalın fiil şimdiki yeteneği, could + yalın fiil geçmişteki yeteneği anlatır. Olumsuz: can't, couldn't. Can her kişi için aynıdır, -s ve to almaz: she can ski, he can cook. Birinden yardım istemek için Can you ...? ile başla: Can you carry this box? Unutma: can ya da could'dan sonra to gelmez — “He can to play the guitar” değil, “He can play the guitar”.
fa: “I can't swim very well, but when I was a child I could swim for hours.” قاعده: can + شکل سادهٔ فعل یعنی توانایی الان، و could + شکل سادهٔ فعل یعنی توانایی در گذشته. منفی: can't, couldn't. can برای همهٔ شخص‌ها یکی است و ‎-s و to نمی‌گیرد: she can ski, he can cook. برای کمک خواستن با Can you ...? شروع کن: Can you carry this box? یادت باشد: بعد از can یا could، to نمی‌آید — “He can play the guitar”، نه “He can to play the guitar”.

en: Before the main verb, but after am / is / are.
tr: Ana fiilden önce, ama am / is / are'dan sonra.
fa: قبل از فعل اصلی، اما بعد از am / is / are.

en: Put the adverb before every verb, even 'am'.
tr: Zarf her fiilden önce gelir, 'am'den bile.
fa: قید قبل از هر فعلی می‌آید، حتی am.

en: The adverb goes at the start: Never I eat breakfast.
tr: Zarf başa gelir: Never I eat breakfast.
fa: قید اول جمله می‌آید: Never I eat breakfast.

en: “I usually take the bus, but I'm always late on Mondays.” The rule: put always, usually, often, sometimes and never before the main verb, but after am / is / are. From most to least: always, usually, often, sometimes, never. Before the main verb: I often cook, she never drinks coffee. After be: he is usually tired, we are never bored. Never already means not ever, so don't add not to it. Remember: be comes first — “She is often busy”, not “She often is busy”.
tr: “I usually take the bus, but I'm always late on Mondays.” Kural: always, usually, often, sometimes ve never'ı ana fiilin önüne, ama am / is / are'dan sonra koy. Çoktan aza: always, usually, often, sometimes, never. Ana fiilden önce: I often cook, she never drinks coffee. Be'den sonra: he is usually tired, we are never bored. Türkçede “hiç” olumsuz fiille gelir, ama never zaten olumsuzdur, yanına not ekleme. Unutma: önce be gelir — “She often is busy” değil, “She is often busy”.
fa: “I usually take the bus, but I'm always late on Mondays.” قاعده: always، usually، often، sometimes و never را قبل از فعل اصلی بگذار، ولی بعد از am / is / are. از بیشتر به کمتر: always, usually, often, sometimes, never. قبل از فعل اصلی: I often cook, she never drinks coffee. بعد از be: he is usually tired, we are never bored. در فارسی «هیچ‌وقت» با فعل منفی می‌آید، ولی never خودش منفی است و not نمی‌خواهد. یادت باشد: اول be می‌آید — “She is often busy”، نه “She often is busy”.

en: Happening now: am / is / are + verb-ing.
tr: Şu anda oluyor: am / is / are + fiil-ing.
fa: همین الان در جریان: am / is / are + فعل-ing.

en: For 'right now', use the simple present: I go now.
tr: 'Right now' için geniş zaman: I go now.
fa: برای right now حال ساده: I go now.

en: verb-ing works alone, without am / is / are.
tr: fiil-ing tek başına yeter, am / is / are gerekmez.
fa: فعل-ing به‌تنهایی کافی است، بدون am / is / are.

en: “Sorry, I can't talk — I'm cooking dinner.” The rule: am / is / are + verb-ing for something happening now or around now. Forms: I am working, she is working, they are working. Negatives add not: I'm not watching. Questions start with the be verb: What are you doing? It also works for things in progress this week or this month. Spelling: run → running, swim → swimming, have → having, write → writing. Remember: you need both parts — “She is waiting outside”, not “She waiting outside” or “She is wait outside”.
tr: “Sorry, I can't talk — I'm cooking dinner.” Kural: şu anda ya da bu aralar olan bir şey için am / is / are + fiil-ing kullan. Biçimler: I am working, she is working, they are working. Olumsuzda not eklenir: I'm not watching. Soru be fiiliyle başlar: What are you doing? Bu hafta ya da bu ay süren işler için de kullanılır. Yazım: run → running, swim → swimming, have → having, write → writing. Unutma: iki parça da gerekir — “She waiting outside” ya da “She is wait outside” değil, “She is waiting outside”.
fa: “Sorry, I can't talk — I'm cooking dinner.” قاعده: برای کاری که الان یا این روزها در جریان است، am / is / are + فعل با ‎-ing بیاور. شکل‌ها: I am working, she is working, they are working. در منفی not اضافه می‌شود: I'm not watching. سؤال با فعل be شروع می‌شود: What are you doing? این زمان فقط برای همین لحظه نیست؛ برای کاری که این هفته یا این ماه ادامه دارد هم به کار می‌رود. املا: running, swimming, having, writing. یادت باشد: هر دو بخش لازم است — “She is waiting outside”، نه “She waiting outside” یا “She is wait outside”.

en: After a verb or 'to', use me, him, her, us, them.
tr: Fiilden ya da 'to'dan sonra me, him, her, us, them.
fa: بعد از فعل یا to: me، him، her، us، them.

en: Pronouns don't change: give it to she.
tr: Zamirler değişmez: give it to she.
fa: ضمیرها عوض نمی‌شوند: give it to she.

en: Use 'my' and 'his' after a verb: help my.
tr: Fiilden sonra 'my', 'his' kullanılır: help my.
fa: بعد از فعل از my و his استفاده می‌شود: help my.

en: “I called Sara and invited her to dinner.” The rule: after a verb, or after a word like to, for or with, use an object pronoun. Pairs: I → me, he → him, she → her, we → us, they → them. You and it stay the same. The subject does the action and the object receives it: She loves him. He loves her. Don't use my, his or mine here: help me, not help my. Remember: after to and for, use the object form — “This present is for them”, not “This present is for they”.
tr: “I called Sara and invited her to dinner.” Kural: fiilden ya da to, for, with gibi bir kelimeden sonra nesne zamiri kullan. Eşler: I → me, he → him, she → her, we → us, they → them. You ve it değişmez. Özne eylemi yapar, nesne eylemden etkilenir: She loves him. He loves her. Burada my, his ya da mine kullanma: help me, help my değil. Türkçede “onu” ve “ona” erkek ve kadın için aynıdır; İngilizcede ise him ve her ayrıdır. Unutma: to ve for'dan sonra nesne biçimi gelir — “This present is for they” değil, “This present is for them”.
fa: “I called Sara and invited her to dinner.” قاعده: بعد از فعل، یا بعد از کلمه‌ای مثل to، for و with، ضمیر مفعولی بیاور. جفت‌ها: I / me, he / him, she / her, we / us, they / them. you و it عوض نمی‌شوند. فاعل کار را انجام می‌دهد و کار روی مفعول انجام می‌شود: She loves him. He loves her. این‌جا my، his یا mine نیاور: help me، نه help my. در فارسی «او» برای زن و مرد یکی است، ولی در انگلیسی him و her فرق دارند. یادت باشد: بعد از to و for شکل مفعولی می‌آید — “This present is for them”، نه “This present is for they”.

en: Orders drop the subject: base verb, or Don't + verb.
tr: Emirde özne düşer: yalın fiil ya da Don't + fiil.
fa: در دستور فاعل حذف می‌شود: فعل ساده یا Don't + فعل.

en: Orders start with 'You': You turn left.
tr: Emir 'You' ile başlar: You turn left.
fa: دستور با You شروع می‌شود: You turn left.

en: A negative order uses 'Not' or 'No' + verb.
tr: Olumsuz emir 'Not' ya da 'No' + fiil ile yapılır.
fa: دستور منفی با Not یا No + فعل ساخته می‌شود.

en: “Take the second street on the left, then cross the bridge.” The rule: for instructions, orders and warnings, start with the base verb and leave out you. Examples: Open your books. Turn right. Be careful. For a negative, use Don't + base verb: Don't touch that. Don't be late. Not or No on its own is wrong here. To sound polite, add please at the start or at the end, with no to: Please come in. Come in, please. Remember: no -ing and no to — “Wait here, please”, not “Waiting here, please” or “To wait here, please”.
tr: “Take the second street on the left, then cross the bridge.” Kural: talimat, emir ve uyarılar için cümleye yalın fiille başla ve you'yu kullanma. Örnekler: Open your books. Turn right. Be careful. Olumsuz için Don't + yalın fiil kullan: Don't touch that. Don't be late. Burada tek başına Not ya da No yanlıştır. Kibar olmak için please'i başa ya da sona ekle, to kullanma: Please come in. Come in, please. Unutma: -ing ve to yok — “Waiting here, please” ya da “To wait here, please” değil, “Wait here, please”.
fa: “Take the second street on the left, then cross the bridge.” قاعده: برای راهنمایی، دستور و هشدار، جمله را با شکل سادهٔ فعل شروع کن و you را نیاور. نمونه‌ها: Open your books. Turn right. Be careful. برای منفی، Don't + شکل سادهٔ فعل بیاور: Don't touch that. Don't be late. این‌جا Not یا No به‌تنهایی غلط است. برای مؤدبانه شدن، please را اول یا آخر جمله بگذار، بدون to: Please come in. Come in, please. یادت باشد: نه ‎-ing، نه to — “Wait here, please”، نه “Waiting here, please” یا “To wait here, please”.

en: A finished time word, like yesterday, means past simple.
tr: Bitmiş zaman sözcüğü (yesterday gibi) = past simple.
fa: کلمهٔ زمانِ تمام‌شده مثل yesterday یعنی گذشتهٔ ساده.

en: 'Have seen' works with any time word, even yesterday.
tr: 'Have seen' her zaman sözcüğüyle olur, yesterday ile bile.
fa: have seen با هر کلمهٔ زمانی می‌آید، حتی yesterday.

en: 'So far' and 'twice' need the past simple.
tr: 'So far' ve 'twice' past simple ister.
fa: so far و twice گذشتهٔ ساده می‌خواهند.

en: Compare “I have lost my keys” (I still can't find them) with “I lost my keys yesterday” (a finished time). The rule: if you say or mean a finished time, use the past simple; if the time is open or not given, use have / has + past participle. Finished times are words like yesterday, last week, in 2010 and two days ago. Open times are ever, never, already, yet, so far and this week. Remember: a question with when asks for a finished time, so it takes the past simple — “When did you arrive?”, not “When have you arrived?”.
tr: “I have lost my keys” (anahtarlarımı hâlâ bulamıyorum) ile “I lost my keys yesterday” (bitmiş bir zaman) cümlelerini karşılaştır. Türkçede ikisi de “kaybettim” olur; İngilizcede ise seçim zamana bağlıdır. Kural: bitmiş bir zaman söylüyorsan ya da kastediyorsan past simple kullan; zaman açıksa ya da hiç söylenmiyorsa have / has + past participle kullan. Bitmiş zamanlar yesterday, last week, in 2010 ve two days ago gibi kelimelerdir. Açık zamanlar ise ever, never, already, yet, so far ve this week. Unutma: when ile sorulan soru bitmiş bir zamanı sorar, bu yüzden past simple ister — “When have you arrived?” değil, “When did you arrive?”.
fa: “I have lost my keys” (هنوز پیدایشان نکرده‌ام) را با “I lost my keys yesterday” (یک زمانِ تمام‌شده) مقایسه کن. قاعده: اگر زمانِ تمام‌شده‌ای را می‌گویی یا در ذهنت داری، گذشتهٔ ساده بگذار؛ اگر زمان باز است یا گفته نمی‌شود، have / has + اسم مفعول بگذار. زمان‌های تمام‌شده کلمه‌هایی مثل yesterday، last week، in 2010 و two days ago هستند. زمان‌های باز ever، never، already، yet، so far و this week هستند. یادت باشد: سؤالی که با when شروع می‌شود دنبال یک زمانِ تمام‌شده است، پس گذشتهٔ ساده می‌خواهد — “When did you arrive?”، نه “When have you arrived?”.

en: A starting point takes since; a length of time takes for.
tr: since = başlangıç noktası; for = süre.
fa: since = نقطهٔ شروع؛ for = طول مدت.

en: 'since' goes with a number of years: since five years.
tr: 'since' yıl sayısıyla gelir: since five years.
fa: since با تعداد سال می‌آید: since five years.

en: 'for' goes with a date or a year: for 2019.
tr: 'for' tarih ya da yılla gelir: for 2019.
fa: for با تاریخ یا سال می‌آید: for 2019.

en: “I've lived here since May” and “I've lived here for five months” say the same thing in two ways. The rule: since + the starting point, for + the length of time. With since: since 2019, since Monday, since I was a child. With for: for two hours, for five years, for a long time. Both usually go with the present perfect, because the action started in the past and is still true now. Remember: ago is different — it counts back from now and takes the past simple: “I moved here five months ago”.
tr: “I've lived here since May” ve “I've lived here for five months” aynı şeyi iki farklı yolla söyler. Kural: since + başlangıç noktası, for + süre. Since ile: since 2019, since Monday, since I was a child. For ile: for two hours, for five years, for a long time. İkisi de genelde present perfect ile gelir, çünkü eylem geçmişte başlamış ve hâlâ sürüyor. Türkçede hem “mayıstan beri” hem “beş aydan beri” denebildiği için since ile for kolayca karışır. Unutma: ago farklıdır — şimdiden geriye sayar ve past simple ister: “I moved here five months ago”.
fa: “I've lived here since May” و “I've lived here for five months” یک چیز را به دو شکل می‌گویند. قاعده: since + نقطهٔ شروع، for + طول مدت. با since: since 2019, since Monday, since I was a child. با for: for two hours, for five years, for a long time. هر دو معمولاً با present perfect می‌آیند، چون کار در گذشته شروع شده و هنوز ادامه دارد. در فارسی هم «از ماه مه» می‌گوییم و هم «از پنج ماه پیش»، برای همین since و for راحت قاطی می‌شوند. یادت باشد: ago فرق دارد — از الان به عقب می‌شمارد و گذشتهٔ ساده می‌خواهد: “I moved here five months ago”.

en: If + present simple, then will + verb.
tr: If + geniş zaman, sonra will + fiil.
fa: If + حال ساده، سپس will + فعل.

en: Both halves take 'will': if it will rain, I will stay.
tr: İki taraf da 'will' alır: if it will rain, I will stay.
fa: هر دو بخش will می‌گیرند: if it will rain, I will stay.

en: The result part uses 'would', not 'will'.
tr: Sonuç kısmı 'will' değil 'would' alır.
fa: بخش نتیجه would می‌گیرد، نه will.

en: “If the bus is late, I'll take a taxi” talks about a real possibility in the future. The rule: if + present simple, then will + base verb. The if-part is about the future too, but it stays in the present simple. Words that work the same way: when, as soon as, before, after. You can put either part first; use a comma only when the if-part comes first. Remember: no will straight after if — “If I see Ali, I'll give him your message”, not “If I will see Ali, I'll give him your message”.
tr: “If the bus is late, I'll take a taxi” gelecekteki gerçek bir ihtimalden söz eder. Kural: if + present simple, ardından will + yalın fiil. If kısmı da geleceği anlatır ama present simple'da kalır. Aynı şekilde çalışan kelimeler: when, as soon as, before, after. İki kısımdan istediğini başa koyabilirsin; virgül sadece if kısmı baştaysa gelir. Unutma: if'ten hemen sonra will gelmez — “If I will see Ali, I'll give him your message” değil, “If I see Ali, I'll give him your message”.
fa: “If the bus is late, I'll take a taxi” دربارهٔ یک احتمال واقعی در آینده است. قاعده: if + حال ساده، بعد will + شکل سادهٔ فعل. بخش if هم دربارهٔ آینده است، ولی در حال ساده می‌ماند. کلمه‌هایی که همین‌طور کار می‌کنند: when, as soon as, before, after. هر کدام از دو بخش را می‌توانی اول بیاوری؛ ویرگول فقط وقتی لازم است که بخش if اول بیاید. یادت باشد: بلافاصله بعد از if فعل will نمی‌آید — “If I see Ali, I'll give him your message”، نه “If I will see Ali, I'll give him your message”.

en: Bare verb after must and should; only 'have to' keeps 'to'.
tr: must / should + yalın fiil; 'to' sadece 'have to'da.
fa: must / should + فعل ساده؛ فقط have to «to» دارد.

en: All three take 'to': must to, should to.
tr: Üçü de 'to' alır: must to, should to.
fa: هر سه to می‌گیرند: must to، should to.

en: 'should' is the strongest: it means a law.
tr: 'should' en güçlüsüdür: yasa demektir.
fa: should قوی‌ترین است: یعنی قانون.

en: “You should try the soup” is advice; “You have to pay at the counter” tells you what is required. The rule: must and should take the base verb with no to. Have to keeps its to and changes like a normal verb, so it is she has to and did you have to. Use should for advice, have to for rules and laws, and must for a strong obligation that you feel yourself. The table shows how strong each one is. Remember: after must, should, can and will, the next verb has no to — “I must call the bank”, not “I must to call the bank”.
tr: “You should try the soup” bir tavsiyedir; “You have to pay at the counter” ise ne yapman gerektiğini söyler. Kural: must ve should'dan sonra fiil yalın gelir, to yoktur. Have to ise to'sunu korur ve normal bir fiil gibi değişir, yani she has to ve did you have to olur. Tavsiye için should, kurallar ve yasalar için have to, kendi hissettiğin güçlü bir zorunluluk için must kullan. Tabloda her birinin ne kadar güçlü olduğu görünüyor. Unutma: must, should, can ve will'den sonra gelen fiil to almaz — “I must to call the bank” değil, “I must call the bank”.
fa: “You should try the soup” یک توصیه است؛ “You have to pay at the counter” می‌گوید چه کاری لازم است. قاعده: بعد از must و should شکل سادهٔ فعل می‌آید، بدون to. اما have to «to»یش را نگه می‌دارد و مثل یک فعل معمولی عوض می‌شود، یعنی she has to و did you have to. برای توصیه should، برای قانون و مقررات have to، و برای اجباری قوی که خودت حس می‌کنی must بگذار. جدول نشان می‌دهد هر کدام چقدر قوی است. یادت باشد: بعد از must، should، can و will فعل بعدی to نمی‌گیرد — “I must call the bank”، نه “I must to call the bank”.

en: was / were + past participle: the window was broken.
tr: Edilgen = was / were + 3. hâl: was broken.
fa: مجهول = was / were + اسم مفعول: was broken.

en: Passive needs only the participle: the window broken.
tr: Edilgen için sadece 3. hâl yeter: the window broken.
fa: مجهول فقط اسم مفعول می‌خواهد: the window broken.

en: After was / were, use the base verb: was sing.
tr: was / were'den sonra yalın fiil: was sing.
fa: بعد از was / were فعل ساده: was sing.

en: “Coffee is grown in Brazil” and “My bike was stolen” focus on the thing, not on the person who did it. The rule: be + past participle. Change be for the time: is / are for now and always, was / were for the past. Past participles: made, built, given, taken, found. Add by + the person only when it matters who did it. Remember: never drop be — “The bridge was built in 1990”, not “The bridge built in 1990”.
tr: “Coffee is grown in Brazil” ve “My bike was stolen” işi yapan kişiye değil, şeyin kendisine odaklanır. Kural: be + past participle. Be'yi zamana göre değiştir: şimdi ve her zaman için is / are, geçmiş için was / were. Past participle örnekleri: made, built, given, taken, found. İşi kimin yaptığı önemliyse by + kişi ekle. Türkçede edilgen tek bir ekle yapılır (yapıldı, çalındı), İngilizcede ise be şarttır. Unutma: be'yi asla atlama — “The bridge built in 1990” değil, “The bridge was built in 1990”.
fa: “Coffee is grown in Brazil” و “My bike was stolen” روی خودِ آن چیز تمرکز می‌کنند، نه روی کسی که کار را کرده. قاعده: be + اسم مفعول. فعل be را با زمان عوض کن: برای حال و همیشه is / are و برای گذشته was / were. چند اسم مفعول: made, built, given, taken, found. فقط وقتی مهم است چه کسی کار را کرده، by + آن شخص را اضافه کن. یادت باشد: be را هیچ‌وقت حذف نکن — “The bridge was built in 1990”، نه “The bridge built in 1990”.

en: People take who, things take which; that fits both.
tr: who = kişiler, which = şeyler, that = ikisi de.
fa: who = آدم‌ها، which = چیزها، that = هر دو.

en: 'which' works for people too: the man which called.
tr: 'which' kişiler için de olur: the man which called.
fa: which برای آدم‌ها هم می‌شود: the man which called.

en: Keep an extra pronoun: the house which I lived in it.
tr: Fazladan zamir kalır: the house which I lived in it.
fa: ضمیر اضافه می‌ماند: the house which I lived in it.

en: “I have a neighbour who grows tomatoes” puts two ideas into one sentence. The rule: who for people, which for things, that for both. Use whose for possession: the man whose car is outside. The relative word takes the place of he, she or it, so don't add another pronoun after it. If the clause needs a preposition, put it at the end: the flat which I live in. Remember: which is never for a person — “the nurse who helped me”, not “the nurse which helped me”.
tr: “I have a neighbour who grows tomatoes” iki fikri tek cümlede birleştirir. Kural: who kişiler için, which şeyler için, that ikisi için. Sahiplik için whose kullan: the man whose car is outside. İlgi kelimesi he, she ya da it'in yerini alır, bu yüzden ardından bir zamir daha ekleme. Cümlecik bir edat istiyorsa edatı sona koy: the flat which I live in. Türkçede ilgi cümleciği ismin önüne gelir (domates yetiştiren komşum), İngilizcede ise ismin arkasından who ya da which ile gelir. Unutma: which hiçbir zaman bir insan için kullanılmaz — “the nurse which helped me” değil, “the nurse who helped me”.
fa: “I have a neighbour who grows tomatoes” دو ایده را در یک جمله می‌آورد. قاعده: who برای آدم‌ها، which برای چیزها و that برای هر دو. برای مالکیت whose بگذار: the man whose car is outside. کلمهٔ موصولی جای he، she یا it را می‌گیرد، پس بعدش ضمیر دیگری نیاور. اگر جمله حرف اضافه لازم دارد، آن را آخر بگذار: the flat which I live in. در فارسی برای آدم و چیز فقط «که» داریم، ولی انگلیسی بین who و which فرق می‌گذارد. یادت باشد: which هیچ‌وقت برای آدم نیست — “the nurse who helped me”، نه “the nurse which helped me”.

en: Past habit, now over: used to + base verb.
tr: Bitmiş geçmiş alışkanlık: used to + yalın fiil.
fa: عادت گذشته که تمام شده: used to + فعل ساده.

en: 'use to' is the normal form: I use to smoke.
tr: Normal biçim 'use to'dur: I use to smoke.
fa: شکل عادی use to است: I use to smoke.

en: 'be used to' means a past habit: she is used to live here.
tr: 'be used to' geçmiş alışkanlıktır: she is used to live here.
fa: be used to یعنی عادت گذشته: she is used to live here.

en: “My grandmother used to walk to school” means she did it every day in the past, but she doesn't now. The rule: used to + base verb is for past habits and past states that are not true now. It never changes for the person: I used to, she used to, they used to. In negatives and questions, did carries the past, so the d goes: didn't use to, Did you use to ...? Don't mix it up with be used to + -ing, which means that something feels normal to you. Remember: in a positive sentence the d always stays — “We used to live by the sea”, not “We use to live by the sea”.
tr: “My grandmother used to walk to school” demek, eskiden her gün okula yürürdü ama artık yürümüyor demek. Kural: used to + yalın fiil, geçmişteki ve artık geçerli olmayan alışkanlıklar ve durumlar içindir. Kişiye göre hiç değişmez: I used to, she used to, they used to. Olumsuz ve soru cümlelerinde geçmişi did taşır, bu yüzden d düşer: didn't use to, Did you use to ...? Bunu be used to + -ing ile karıştırma; o “bir şeye alışkın olmak” demektir. Türkçedeki “-erdi” eki (eskiden yürürdü) bu anlamı karşılar, ama İngilizcede iki kelimelik ayrı bir yapı gerekir. Unutma: olumlu cümlede d hep kalır — “We use to live by the sea” değil, “We used to live by the sea”.
fa: “My grandmother used to walk to school” یعنی مادربزرگم قبلاً هر روز پیاده به مدرسه می‌رفت، ولی حالا دیگر نه. قاعده: used to + شکل سادهٔ فعل برای عادت‌ها و حالت‌های گذشته است که الان دیگر درست نیستند. با فاعل عوض نمی‌شود: I used to, she used to, they used to. در جملهٔ منفی و سؤالی did گذشته را نشان می‌دهد، پس d می‌افتد: didn't use to, Did you use to ...? آن را با be used to + ‎-ing قاطی نکن؛ معنی آن «به چیزی عادت داشتن» است. در فارسی همین معنی را با ماضی استمراری می‌گوییم («می‌رفت»)، ولی در انگلیسی یک ساختار دوکلمه‌ای لازم است. یادت باشد: در جملهٔ مثبت d همیشه می‌ماند — “We used to live by the sea”، نه “We use to live by the sea”.

en: The first verb decides: enjoy + -ing, want + to.
tr: İlk fiil karar verir: enjoy + -ing, want + to.
fa: فعل اول تصمیم می‌گیرد: enjoy + ‎-ing، want + to.

en: After any verb, use 'to': enjoy to swim.
tr: Her fiilden sonra 'to': enjoy to swim.
fa: بعد از هر فعلی to: enjoy to swim.

en: The second verb is always bare: wants find.
tr: İkinci fiil hep yalındır: wants find.
fa: فعل دوم همیشه ساده است: wants find.

en: “I enjoy cooking” but “I want to cook”: the first verb decides the form of the second. The rule: some verbs are followed by -ing and others by to + verb. Verbs + -ing: enjoy, avoid, finish, mind, suggest. Verbs + to: want, decide, hope, plan, agree. As a rough guide, to + verb often looks ahead (plans, hopes), while -ing often names an activity. Stop changes the meaning: “I stopped smoking” means I don't smoke now. Remember: after enjoy, the next verb takes -ing — “She enjoys walking to work”, not “She enjoys to walk to work”.
tr: “I enjoy cooking” ama “I want to cook”: ikinci fiilin biçimine ilk fiil karar verir. Kural: bazı fiillerden sonra -ing, bazılarından sonra to + fiil gelir. Ardından -ing gelen fiiller: enjoy, avoid, finish, mind, suggest. Ardından to gelen fiiller: want, decide, hope, plan, agree. Kabaca, to + fiil çoğu zaman ileriye bakar (plan, umut), -ing ise bir etkinliğe ad verir. Stop anlamı değiştirir: “I stopped smoking” artık sigara içmiyorum demektir. Türkçede ikisi de “-mek / -meyi” ile söylendiği için (yemek yapmayı severim, yemek yapmak istiyorum) bu ayrım doğal gelmez. Unutma: enjoy'dan sonraki fiil -ing alır — “She enjoys to walk to work” değil, “She enjoys walking to work”.
fa: “I enjoy cooking” ولی “I want to cook”: فعل اول تعیین می‌کند فعل دوم چه شکلی باشد. قاعده: بعد از بعضی فعل‌ها ‎-ing می‌آید و بعد از بعضی دیگر to + فعل. فعل‌هایی که ‎-ing می‌گیرند: enjoy, avoid, finish, mind, suggest. فعل‌هایی که to می‌گیرند: want, decide, hope, plan, agree. به‌طور کلی to + فعل بیشتر به آینده نگاه می‌کند (برنامه، امید) و ‎-ing بیشتر اسم یک فعالیت است. فعل stop معنی را عوض می‌کند: “I stopped smoking” یعنی دیگر سیگار نمی‌کشم. یادت باشد: بعد از enjoy فعل بعدی ‎-ing می‌گیرد — “She enjoys walking to work”، نه “She enjoys to walk to work”.

en: Positive sentence, negative tag; reuse the same helper verb.
tr: Olumlu cümle, olumsuz kuyruk; aynı yardımcı fiil.
fa: جملهٔ مثبت، دنبالهٔ منفی؛ همان فعل کمکی.

en: 'isn't it?' fits the end of any sentence.
tr: 'isn't it?' her cümlenin sonuna uyar.
fa: isn't it? به آخر هر جمله‌ای می‌خورد.

en: A positive sentence takes a positive tag: It's cold, is it?
tr: Olumlu cümleye olumlu kuyruk: It's cold, is it?
fa: جملهٔ مثبت دنبالهٔ مثبت می‌گیرد: It's cold, is it?

en: “You're from Izmir, aren't you?” checks something you think is true. The rule: a positive sentence takes a negative tag, and a negative sentence takes a positive tag. Use the same helper verb as the sentence (is, are, can, have, will) and the subject as a pronoun. With no helper verb, use do, does or did: You work here, don't you? She called, didn't she? Common tags: isn't it, aren't they, won't you, wasn't he. Remember: the tag repeats the subject, so it isn't always it — “Your parents are coming, aren't they?”, not “Your parents are coming, isn't it?”.
tr: “You're from Izmir, aren't you?” doğru olduğunu düşündüğün bir şeyi teyit etmek için sorulur. Kural: olumlu cümle olumsuz bir kuyruk soru alır, olumsuz cümle ise olumlu. Cümledeki yardımcı fiili (is, are, can, have, will) ve özneyi zamir olarak tekrarla. Yardımcı fiil yoksa do, does ya da did kullan: You work here, don't you? She called, didn't she? Sık görülenler: isn't it, aren't they, won't you, wasn't he. Türkçede “değil mi” hiç değişmez, İngilizcede ise kuyruk soru özneye ve fiile göre değişir. Unutma: kuyruk soru özneyi tekrar eder, yani her zaman it değildir — “Your parents are coming, isn't it?” değil, “Your parents are coming, aren't they?”.
fa: “You're from Izmir, aren't you?” برای تأیید چیزی است که فکر می‌کنی درست است. قاعده: جملهٔ مثبت دنبالهٔ منفی می‌گیرد و جملهٔ منفی دنبالهٔ مثبت. همان فعل کمکیِ جمله (is, are, can, have, will) را بیاور و فاعل را به شکل ضمیر تکرار کن. اگر فعل کمکی نیست، do، does یا did بگذار: You work here, don't you? She called, didn't she? دنباله‌های رایج: isn't it, aren't they, won't you, wasn't he. در فارسی «نه؟» یا «مگه نه؟» هیچ‌وقت عوض نمی‌شود، ولی در انگلیسی دنباله با فاعل و فعل عوض می‌شود. یادت باشد: دنباله فاعل را تکرار می‌کند، پس همیشه it نیست — “Your parents are coming, aren't they?”، نه “Your parents are coming, isn't it?”.

en: After 'said', the tense steps back: is → was.
tr: 'said'den sonra zaman bir adım geri gider: is → was.
fa: بعد از said زمان یک قدم عقب می‌رود: is ← was.

en: After 'said', keep the tense exactly as spoken.
tr: 'said'den sonra zaman söylendiği gibi kalır.
fa: بعد از said زمان همان‌طور که گفته شده می‌ماند.

en: 'said' moves the verb forward: is → has been.
tr: 'said' fiili ileri taşır: is → has been.
fa: said فعل را جلو می‌برد: is ← has been.

en: When you tell someone what another person said, the verb usually moves one step back: “I'm tired” becomes “Ali said he was tired”. The rule: after said or told me, move the tense one step into the past. Common changes: am / is → was, are → were, can → could, will → would. The present simple becomes the past simple: “We need help” → They said they needed help. Pronouns change too: I becomes he or she, and my becomes his or her. Remember: if said is in the past, the reported verb usually goes back too — “Omar said the shop was closed”, not “Omar said the shop is closed”.
tr: Birinin söylediğini başkasına aktarırken fiil genelde bir adım geriye gider: “I'm tired” cümlesi “Ali said he was tired” olur. Kural: said ya da told me'den sonra zamanı bir adım geçmişe al. Sık değişimler: am / is → was, are → were, can → could, will → would. Present simple, past simple olur: “We need help” → They said they needed help. Zamirler de değişir: I yerine he ya da she, my yerine his ya da her gelir. Türkçede “yorgunum dedi” deriz ve fiil aynı kalır, İngilizcede ise genelde geriye kayar. Unutma: said geçmişteyse aktarılan fiil de genelde geriye gider — “Omar said the shop is closed” değil, “Omar said the shop was closed”.
fa: وقتی حرف کسی را برای دیگری نقل می‌کنی، فعل معمولاً یک قدم به عقب می‌رود: “I'm tired” می‌شود “Ali said he was tired”. قاعده: بعد از said یا told me زمان فعل را یک قدم به گذشته ببر. تغییرهای رایج: am و is می‌شوند was، are می‌شود were، can می‌شود could و will می‌شود would. حال ساده می‌شود گذشتهٔ ساده: “We need help” می‌شود They said they needed help. ضمیرها هم عوض می‌شوند: I می‌شود he یا she، و my می‌شود his یا her. در فارسی می‌گوییم «گفت خسته است» و زمان عوض نمی‌شود، ولی در انگلیسی معمولاً عقب می‌رود. یادت باشد: وقتی said در گذشته است، فعل نقل‌شده هم معمولاً عقب می‌رود — “Omar said the shop was closed”، نه “Omar said the shop is closed”.

en: Unreal now: if + past simple, would + verb.
tr: Şimdi gerçek dışı: if + past simple, would + fiil.
fa: غیرواقعیِ حال: if + گذشتهٔ ساده، would + فعل.

en: 'would' goes in both halves: if I would have time.
tr: 'would' iki tarafta da olur: if I would have time.
fa: would در هر دو بخش می‌آید: if I would have time.

en: The if-part uses the present: if I am you, I would…
tr: If kısmı şimdiki zaman alır: if I am you, I would…
fa: بخش if حال می‌گیرد: if I am you, I would…

en: “If my flat had a balcony, I would grow tomatoes.” It doesn't have one: the situation is imagined. The rule: for an unreal or unlikely situation now or in the future, use if + past simple, then would + base verb. The past form here is not about the past; it only shows that the situation is not real. With be, use were for every person: if I were, if she were. For advice, say If I were you, I would ... You can start with either half; use a comma only when the if-part comes first: I'd be happier if I lived by the sea. Questions put would first: What would you do if you lost your phone? Remember: no would in the if-part — “If we knew the answer, we would tell you”, not “If we would know the answer, we would tell you”.
tr: “If my flat had a balcony, I would grow tomatoes.” Dairemin balkonu yok: durum hayalî. Kural: şimdi ya da gelecekte gerçek olmayan ya da pek olası olmayan bir durum için if + past simple, ardından would + yalın fiil kullan. Buradaki geçmiş biçim geçmişi anlatmaz, sadece durumun gerçek olmadığını gösterir. Be fiilinde her kişi için were kullan: if I were, if she were. Öğüt vermek için If I were you, I would ... de. İki kısımdan istediğini başa koyabilirsin; virgül sadece if kısmı baştaysa gelir: I'd be happier if I lived by the sea. Soruda would başa gelir: What would you do if you lost your phone? Unutma: if kısmında would olmaz — “If we would know the answer, we would tell you” değil, “If we knew the answer, we would tell you”.
fa: “If my flat had a balcony, I would grow tomatoes.” آپارتمانم بالکن ندارد: این موقعیت خیالی است. قاعده: برای موقعیتی که الان یا در آینده واقعی نیست یا بعید است، if + گذشتهٔ ساده بیاور، بعد would + شکل سادهٔ فعل. این شکل گذشته دربارهٔ گذشته نیست؛ فقط نشان می‌دهد موقعیت واقعی نیست. با be برای همهٔ شخص‌ها were بیاور: if I were, if she were. برای نصیحت بگو If I were you, I would ... هر کدام از دو بخش را می‌توانی اول بیاوری؛ ویرگول فقط وقتی لازم است که بخش if اول بیاید: I'd be happier if I lived by the sea. در سؤال would اول می‌آید: What would you do if you lost your phone? یادت باشد: در بخش if، would نمی‌آید — “If we knew the answer, we would tell you”، نه “If we would know the answer, we would tell you”.

en: Past regret: if + had + participle, would have + participle.
tr: Geçmiş pişmanlık: if + had + 3. hâl, would have + 3. hâl.
fa: حسرت گذشته: if + had + اسم مفعول، would have + اسم مفعول.

en: The result uses plain 'would': if I had known, I would go.
tr: Sonuç yalın 'would' alır: if I had known, I would go.
fa: نتیجه would ساده می‌گیرد: if I had known, I would go.

en: Use 'will have' for the result: she will have passed.
tr: Sonuç için 'will have': she will have passed.
fa: برای نتیجه will have: she will have passed.

en: “If we had left ten minutes earlier, we would have caught the train.” We didn't leave early, and we missed it. The rule: for an imagined past, use if + had + past participle, then would have + past participle. Both halves stay in the past. For a negative, use hadn't: If you hadn't called, I would have overslept. In speech, both had and would shorten to 'd: If they'd invited us, we'd have gone. The first 'd is had; the second is would. Remember: the result needs would have — “If the shop had been open, I would have bought it”, not “If the shop had been open, I would buy it”.
tr: “If we had left ten minutes earlier, we would have caught the train.” Erken çıkmadık ve treni kaçırdık. Kural: hayal edilen bir geçmiş için if + had + past participle, ardından would have + past participle kullan. İki kısım da geçmişte kalır. Olumsuz için hadn't kullan: If you hadn't called, I would have overslept. Konuşurken hem had hem would 'd olarak kısalır: If they'd invited us, we'd have gone. İlk 'd had, ikincisi would'dur. Unutma: sonuç kısmı would have ister — “If the shop had been open, I would buy it” değil, “If the shop had been open, I would have bought it”.
fa: “If we had left ten minutes earlier, we would have caught the train.” زود راه نیفتادیم و به قطار نرسیدیم. قاعده: برای گذشته‌ای خیالی، if + had + اسم مفعول بیاور، بعد would have + اسم مفعول. هر دو بخش در گذشته می‌مانند. برای منفی hadn't بیاور: If you hadn't called, I would have overslept. در گفتار، هم had و هم would به 'd کوتاه می‌شوند: If they'd invited us, we'd have gone. اولی had است و دومی would. یادت باشد: نتیجه would have می‌خواهد — “If the shop had been open, I would have bought it”، نه “If the shop had been open, I would buy it”.

en: modal + be + past participle: will be finished.
tr: modal + be + 3. hâl: will be finished.
fa: فعل وجهی + be + اسم مفعول: will be finished.

en: After 'will', drop 'be': the project will finished.
tr: 'will'den sonra 'be' atılır: the project will finished.
fa: بعد از will، be حذف می‌شود: the project will finished.

en: 'is being' describes the past, not right now.
tr: 'is being' şu anı değil geçmişi anlatır.
fa: is being گذشته را می‌گوید، نه همین الان را.

en: “Sorry, the lift is being repaired” tells you what is happening to the lift, not who is doing it. The rule: the passive is be + past participle, and be carries the tense. Now: is / are being + participle (the road is being cleaned). Past: was / were + participle (the tickets were checked). After a modal (will, must, can, might, should), be stays in its base form: will be sent, can be paid, must be signed. Use the passive when the action matters more than the person, as in notices, news and work emails. Remember: never drop be after a modal — “Your parcel will be delivered on Monday”, not “Your parcel will delivered on Monday”.
tr: “Sorry, the lift is being repaired” asansöre ne olduğunu söyler, onu kimin tamir ettiğini değil. Kural: edilgen yapı be + past participle'dır ve zamanı be taşır. Şu an: is / are being + participle (the road is being cleaned). Geçmiş: was / were + participle (the tickets were checked). Bir modal fiilden (will, must, can, might, should) sonra be yalın kalır: will be sent, can be paid, must be signed. Eylem, onu yapan kişiden daha önemliyse edilgen yapıyı kullan; duyurularda, haberlerde ve iş e-postalarında çok görülür. Unutma: modal fiilden sonra be asla düşmez — “Your parcel will delivered on Monday” değil, “Your parcel will be delivered on Monday”.
fa: “Sorry, the lift is being repaired” می‌گوید چه اتفاقی برای آسانسور می‌افتد، نه اینکه چه کسی تعمیرش می‌کند. قاعده: مجهول یعنی be + اسم مفعول، و زمان را be نشان می‌دهد. الان: is / are being + اسم مفعول (the road is being cleaned). گذشته: was / were + اسم مفعول (the tickets were checked). بعد از فعل‌های وجهی (will، must، can، might، should)، be به شکل ساده می‌ماند: will be sent، can be paid، must be signed. وقتی خودِ کار مهم‌تر از کسی است که آن را انجام می‌دهد، مجهول را به کار ببر؛ در اطلاعیه‌ها، خبرها و ایمیل‌های کاری زیاد دیده می‌شود. یادت باشد: بعد از فعل وجهی be هیچ‌وقت نمی‌افتد — “Your parcel will be delivered on Monday”، نه “Your parcel will delivered on Monday”.

en: A retold question keeps statement order and shifts back.
tr: Aktarılan soru düz cümle sırasını alır ve geri kayar.
fa: سؤال نقل‌شده ترتیب خبری دارد و یک زمان عقب می‌رود.

en: Keep the question order: he asked where was I going.
tr: Soru sırası kalır: he asked where was I going.
fa: ترتیب سؤالی می‌ماند: he asked where was I going.

en: Commands are reported with the base verb: told me close.
tr: Emirler yalın fiille aktarılır: told me close.
fa: دستورها با فعل ساده نقل می‌شوند: told me close.

en: If a colleague asks “Can you help me?”, you later report it as “She asked if I could help her.” The rule: in a reported question, use statement word order and move the tense one step back. With a question word, keep it: asked where the bank was, asked what time the shop opened. With a yes/no question, add if or whether: asked if I was hungry. Tense steps: am / is → was, are → were, can → could, will → would, present simple → past simple. For orders and requests, use tell or ask + person + to + verb, and not to for a negative: told me to wait, asked us not to shout. Remember: a reported question has no do / did and no question mark — “He asked where I lived”, not “He asked where did I live?”.
tr: Bir iş arkadaşın “Can you help me?” diye sorarsa, bunu sonra “She asked if I could help her.” diye aktarırsın. Kural: aktarılan soruda düz cümle sırasını kullan ve zamanı bir adım geriye kaydır. Soru kelimesi varsa onu koru: asked where the bank was, asked what time the shop opened. Evet/hayır sorusunda if ya da whether ekle: asked if I was hungry. Zaman adımları: am / is → was, are → were, can → could, will → would, present simple → past simple. Emir ve ricalarda tell ya da ask + kişi + to + fiil kullan, olumsuzu için not to: told me to wait, asked us not to shout. Unutma: aktarılan soruda do / did ve soru işareti olmaz — “He asked where did I live?” değil, “He asked where I lived”.
fa: اگر همکارت بپرسد “Can you help me?”، بعداً آن را این‌طور نقل می‌کنی: “She asked if I could help her.” قاعده: در سؤالِ نقل‌شده ترتیب جملهٔ خبری را به کار ببر و زمان را یک قدم به عقب ببر. اگر کلمهٔ پرسشی هست، نگهش دار: asked where the bank was، asked what time the shop opened. در سؤال بله/نه، if یا whether اضافه کن: asked if I was hungry. قدم‌های زمان: am / is / was، are / were، can / could، will / would، و present simple به past simple تبدیل می‌شود. برای دستور و درخواست، tell یا ask + شخص + to + فعل را به کار ببر، و برای منفی not to را: told me to wait، asked us not to shout. یادت باشد: سؤالِ نقل‌شده do / did و علامت سؤال ندارد — “He asked where I lived”، نه “He asked where did I live?”.

en: Past guess: must / might / can't + have + participle.
tr: Geçmiş tahmini: must / might / can't + have + 3. hâl.
fa: حدس دربارهٔ گذشته: must / might / can't + have + اسم مفعول.

en: 'must' + base verb covers the past: she must left.
tr: 'must' + yalın fiil geçmişi de karşılar: she must left.
fa: must + فعل ساده گذشته را هم می‌رساند: she must left.

en: After she / he, say 'might has forgotten'.
tr: she / he'den sonra 'might has forgotten' denir.
fa: بعد از she / he می‌گوییم might has forgotten.

en: “Her lights are off and her car is gone, so she must have gone home early” is a guess about something you didn't see. The rule: modal + have + past participle is a guess about the past, based on what you can see now. Sure it happened: must have. Sure it didn't happen: can't have or couldn't have. Maybe it happened: might have, may have, could have. The modal never changes, and have always follows it: she must have, they might have. Remember: after the modal comes have, never has — “He might have missed the bus”, not “He might has missed the bus”.
tr: “Her lights are off and her car is gone, so she must have gone home early” cümlesi, görmediğin bir şey hakkında bir tahmindir. Kural: modal + have + past participle, şu an gördüklerine dayanarak geçmiş hakkında yapılan bir tahmindir. Olduğundan eminsen: must have. Olmadığından eminsen: can't have ya da couldn't have. Belki olmuştur: might have, may have, could have. Modal hiç değişmez ve ardından hep have gelir: she must have, they might have. Türkçedeki “-mış olmalı” must have'e, “-mış olamaz” ise can't have'e karşılık gelir. Unutma: modalden sonra has değil have gelir — “He might has missed the bus” değil, “He might have missed the bus”.
fa: “Her lights are off and her car is gone, so she must have gone home early” حدسی است دربارهٔ چیزی که ندیده‌ای. قاعده: فعل وجهی + have + اسم مفعول یعنی حدس دربارهٔ گذشته، بر اساس چیزی که الان می‌بینی. مطمئنی اتفاق افتاده: must have. مطمئنی اتفاق نیفتاده: can't have یا couldn't have. شاید اتفاق افتاده: might have، may have، could have. فعل وجهی هیچ‌وقت عوض نمی‌شود و بعدش همیشه have می‌آید: she must have، they might have. «حتماً رفته» در فارسی همان must have است و «امکان ندارد رفته باشد» همان can't have. یادت باشد: بعد از فعل وجهی has نمی‌آید، فقط have — “He might have missed the bus”، نه “He might has missed the bus”.

en: A negative opener pulls the auxiliary before the subject.
tr: Olumsuz açılış yardımcı fiili öznenin önüne çeker.
fa: آغازگر منفی فعل کمکی را جلوی فاعل می‌کشد.

en: 'Never' first, then normal order: Never I have seen.
tr: Önce 'Never', sonra normal sıra: Never I have seen.
fa: اول Never، بعد ترتیب عادی: Never I have seen.

en: The adverb loses -ly at the front: Rare have I been.
tr: Başa gelen zarf -ly'yi kaybeder: Rare have I been.
fa: قید در ابتدا -ly را از دست می‌دهد: Rare have I been.

en: “Seldom do we get a quiet evening” sounds stronger than “We seldom get a quiet evening”. The rule: when a negative or limiting word starts the sentence, put the auxiliary before the subject, as in a question. Words that do this: never, rarely, seldom, little, not only, not until. With be or a helper verb, just swap: Never have I seen; Not only is the flat small. With no helper verb, add do / does / did and keep the base verb: Seldom does she call; Little did we know. With not until, the swap comes in the second part: Not until the meeting ended did I see the message. Use inversion in formal writing, speeches and stories, not in everyday chat. Remember: the subject comes after the auxiliary — “Rarely does she complain”, not “Rarely she complains”.
tr: “Seldom do we get a quiet evening”, “We seldom get a quiet evening” cümlesinden daha güçlü duyulur. Kural: cümle olumsuz ya da sınırlayıcı bir kelimeyle başlıyorsa yardımcı fiili, soru cümlesindeki gibi öznenin önüne koy. Bunu yapan kelimeler: never, rarely, seldom, little, not only, not until. Be ya da bir yardımcı fiil varsa sadece yer değiştir: Never have I seen; Not only is the flat small. Yardımcı fiil yoksa do / does / did ekle ve fiili yalın bırak: Seldom does she call; Little did we know. Not until ile yer değiştirme cümlenin ikinci kısmında olur: Not until the meeting ended did I see the message. Devrik yapıyı resmi metinlerde, konuşmalarda ve hikâyelerde kullan, günlük sohbette değil. Unutma: özne yardımcı fiilden sonra gelir — “Rarely she complains” değil, “Rarely does she complain”.
fa: “Seldom do we get a quiet evening” از “We seldom get a quiet evening” قوی‌تر شنیده می‌شود. قاعده: وقتی جمله با یک کلمهٔ منفی یا محدودکننده شروع می‌شود، فعل کمکی را مثل جملهٔ سؤالی قبل از فاعل بیاور. کلمه‌هایی که این کار را می‌کنند: never, rarely, seldom, little, not only, not until. اگر be یا یک فعل کمکی هست، فقط جایشان را عوض کن: Never have I seen; Not only is the flat small. اگر فعل کمکی نیست، do / does / did اضافه کن و فعل را ساده نگه دار: Seldom does she call; Little did we know. با not until، جابه‌جایی در بخش دوم جمله است: Not until the meeting ended did I see the message. این جابه‌جایی را در نوشتهٔ رسمی، سخنرانی و داستان به کار ببر، نه در گپ روزمره. یادت باشد: فاعل بعد از فعل کمکی می‌آید — “Rarely does she complain”، نه “Rarely she complains”.

en: The small word changes the meaning: look vs look into.
tr: Küçük sözcük anlamı değiştirir: look / look into.
fa: کلمهٔ کوچک معنا را عوض می‌کند: look در برابر look into.

en: You can drop the particle: I need to look the report.
tr: Edat atılabilir: I need to look the report.
fa: می‌شود حرف اضافه را انداخت: I need to look the report.

en: Any particle fits: come into my keys, put out with him.
tr: Her edat uyar: come into my keys, put out with him.
fa: هر حرف اضافه‌ای می‌خورد: come into my keys، put out with him.

en: “The meeting was called off” and “The meeting was put off” mean different things: cancelled, or moved to later. The rule: a phrasal verb is one unit of meaning, so learn the verb and its particle together, like a new word. Finding and meeting: come across (find by chance), run into (meet by chance), look into (investigate). Problems: get over (recover from), put up with (accept something annoying), get away with (do something wrong and not be punished). Plans and offers: put off (delay), call off (cancel), turn down (refuse, or make quieter). With a pronoun, two-part verbs like call off and turn down go around it (call it off, turn it down); three-part verbs never split (put up with it). Remember: keep every part of the verb — “Can you look into my order?”, not “Can you look my order?”.
tr: “The meeting was called off” ile “The meeting was put off” farklı şeyler söyler: iptal edildi ya da sonraya ertelendi. Kural: phrasal verb tek bir anlam birimidir; fiili ve edatını yeni bir kelime gibi birlikte öğren. Bulmak ve karşılaşmak: come across (tesadüfen bulmak), run into (tesadüfen karşılaşmak), look into (araştırmak). Sorunlar: get over (atlatmak, iyileşmek), put up with (can sıkıcı bir şeye katlanmak), get away with (yanlış bir şey yapıp ceza almamak). Planlar ve teklifler: put off (ertelemek), call off (iptal etmek), turn down (reddetmek ya da sesini kısmak). Nesne bir zamirse call off ve turn down gibi iki parçalı fiiller zamirin iki yanına geçer (call it off, turn it down); üç parçalı fiiller hiç ayrılmaz (put up with it). Unutma: fiilin hiçbir parçasını atlama — “Can you look my order?” değil, “Can you look into my order?”.
fa: “The meeting was called off” و “The meeting was put off” دو معنی متفاوت دارند: لغو شد، یا به بعد افتاد. قاعده: فعل عبارتی یک واحدِ معنایی است، پس فعل و حرفِ همراهش را با هم یاد بگیر، مثل یک کلمهٔ تازه. پیدا کردن و دیدن: come across (اتفاقی پیدا کردن)، run into (اتفاقی کسی را دیدن)، look into (بررسی کردن). مشکل‌ها: get over (پشت سر گذاشتن، خوب شدن)، put up with (تحمل کردنِ چیزی آزاردهنده)، get away with (کار بدی کردن و تنبیه نشدن). برنامه‌ها و پیشنهادها: put off (عقب انداختن)، call off (لغو کردن)، turn down (رد کردن، یا کم کردنِ صدا). اگر مفعول ضمیر باشد، فعل‌های دوتکه مثل call off و turn down دو طرفِ آن می‌آیند (call it off، turn it down)؛ فعل‌های سه‌تکه هیچ‌وقت جدا نمی‌شوند (put up with it). یادت باشد: هیچ تکه‌ای از فعل را جا نینداز — “Can you look into my order?”، نه “Can you look my order?”.

en: Regret now → past simple; regret the past → past perfect.
tr: Şimdi için wish + past; geçmiş için wish + past perfect.
fa: برای حال wish + گذشته؛ برای گذشته wish + گذشتهٔ کامل.

en: 'wish' takes the present: I wish I am taller.
tr: 'wish' şimdiki zaman alır: I wish I am taller.
fa: wish حال می‌گیرد: I wish I am taller.

en: 'If only' + 'would' for a past regret: if only I would tell.
tr: Geçmiş pişmanlık için 'If only' + 'would': if only I would tell.
fa: برای حسرت گذشته If only + would: if only I would tell.

en: “I wish I knew the answer” is about now: you don't know it. The rule: after wish or if only, move the verb one step back into the past. Now: wish + past simple (I wish I had a car, I wish it were Friday) or could (I wish I could drive). Past regret: wish + had + past participle (I wish I had left earlier). To complain about what someone else does, or keeps doing: wish + person + would (I wish you would listen). If only means the same as I wish, only stronger. Remember: no would for your own wish about now — “I wish I spoke French”, not “I wish I would speak French”.
tr: “I wish I knew the answer” şimdiyle ilgilidir: cevabı bilmiyorsun. Kural: wish ya da if only'den sonra fiili bir adım geçmişe kaydır. Şimdi için: wish + past simple (I wish I had a car, I wish it were Friday) ya da could (I wish I could drive). Geçmişteki pişmanlık için: wish + had + past participle (I wish I had left earlier).
